name: Kelita
title: Levite Who Renewed the Covenant
summary: Kelita was a Levite who lived in the period after the Babylonian exile. He is known for being among those who had taken foreign wives and had to separate from them following Ezra's reforms. He also participated in teaching the people the Law and in sealing the covenant under Nehemiah.

keyEvents.title: Among the Levites Who Had Taken Foreign Wives
keyEvents.description: Kelita was one of the Levites who had married foreign women in violation of God's Law and committed to separating from them after Ezra's exhortation.

keyEvents.title: Teaching the People the Law
keyEvents.description: Kelita was among the Levites who helped the people understand the Law when Ezra read it aloud to the entire assembly.

keyEvents.title: Sealing the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Kelita was among the Levites who placed their seal on the renewed covenant with God under Nehemiah's leadership, where the people committed themselves to follow God's Law.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's Public Reading of the Law
keyEvents.description: During the great assembly at the Water Gate, Kelita actively participated in explaining the content of the Law to the people as they stood in their places.

keyEvents.title: The Levites' Prayer and Confession
keyEvents.description: In connection with the great day of repentance following the reading of the Law, the Levites, including Kelita, helped lead the people in prayer and confession of sin.
